method: Every fetched_url in the ledger (archive.org fulltext/inside.php) was re-fetched and the quote compared with the returned 'text' string. BEHERA 2005 GLOSSARY PAIRINGS were checked by box coordinates: search-inside returns each hit's position on the scan leaf; a headword (left column, l≈160-270) and its definition (right column, l≈950+) printed on the same line share the same top coordinate t (within about 10 px). A pairing is 'confirmed' only when the headword's t equals the first line of the definition (or the definition's second line sits one line-height, about 94 px, below it with no other headword between). Unconfirmed pairings are dropped.

element_rulings.bada: what REVISED (re-verified 2026-09-26). The old last sentence 'Some walls have five parts instead, but the oldest temples use three.' overstates Bose: his evidence is the Bhubaneswar temples he dates early by inscription or style, and counts for single early temples differ (the Parasuramesvara verdict notes Ganguly counts two parts). It is also stylistic dating. New text: early temples 'mostly' have three parts; later temples often five, with the middle split by a band. This matches glossary trianga-bada/bada. temple_ids + konark (Mitra 2003 leaf 53).

new_sources.mitra-d-1960: Bibliography confirmed this run: archive.org details page title 'JOURNAL OF THE ASIATIC SOCIETY VOL. 2, NO. 1-4', date 1960, publisher 'ASIATIC SOCIETY, CALCUTTA'. Article byline leaf 9: 'By Debala Mitra'. Running head leaf 20: '12 DEBALA MITBA [VOL. H,' so scan leaf 9 = printed p. 1. The end page and the journal series were not confirmed. No trace of 'Adris Banerji' as author. Used ONLY in anatomy-terms-glossary-mitra1960.json.
